title: The Iranian Revolution
subtitle: From the 1953 coup to the hostage crisis, 1951–1981

intro.title: Oil, a crown and a turban
body: In 1951 Iran was a monarchy with an elected parliament. Its young Shah, Mohammad Reza Pahlavi, had come to the throne in 1941. Its oil, the country's main wealth, was pumped and sold by a British company.

When Prime Minister Mosaddegh nationalised the oil, Britain and the United States helped overthrow him in 1953. The Shah then ruled with growing power: land reform and women's votes, a secret police, and after 1973 a flood of oil money that brought fast growth and high inflation.

In 1978 a protest movement led by the exiled cleric Ayatollah Khomeini, and joined by liberals, leftists, students, merchants and workers, brought the monarchy down. What followed is still argued over. To some it was a popular revolution against a dictator and foreign control. To others it replaced one tyranny with another. This story follows it to the hostage crisis and the start of the war with Iraq.
tips: Press play for a guided tour. The map flies to each event and back out.
Zoom into Tehran to explore the city of 1978: the marches, the squares, the palaces, the prisons and the US embassy.
The Ashura march of December 1978 and Khomeini's return in February 1979 have animated close-ups. Look for the Watch it unfold button.

eras.title: Oil nationalised
eras.text: Mosaddegh takes Iran's oil from a British company. Britain blockades it, and the economy suffers.

eras.title: The Shah restored
eras.text: A coup backed by the CIA and MI6 removes Mosaddegh. The Shah rules with American support and a new secret police.

eras.title: White Revolution
eras.text: Land reform and women's votes from above. Khomeini speaks out, the army fires on the crowds, and he is sent into exile.

eras.title: Oil boom
eras.text: A lavish celebration of monarchy, a quadrupled oil price, a one-party state, inflation and guerrilla attacks.

eras.title: Revolution
eras.text: Mourning ceremonies every forty days, massacres, strikes and marches of millions. The Shah leaves and Khomeini returns.

eras.title: A new order
eras.text: Revolutionary courts, a vote for an Islamic Republic, revolts in the provinces and a struggle over what the revolution means.

eras.title: Hostages and war
eras.text: Students seize the US embassy. A rescue fails, the Shah dies, and Iraq invades. The hostages go home after 444 days.
